text: What is the primary source of data?
options: Data collected from secondary sources
Data collected from primary sources
Data collected from both primary and secondary sources
Data collected from government offices
explanation: Primary data is collected through original observations or experiments. It is collected from the first-hand information. For example, a survey conducted by a researcher to collect information about the consumer behaviour.

text: Which of the following is an example of a census method?
options: Conducting a survey of 1000 people in a city
Conducting a survey of all the people in a country
Conducting a survey of 50 people in a village
Conducting a survey of all the people in a state
correctAnswer: Conducting a survey of all the people in a country
explanation: A census is a method of collecting data from the entire population. It is a complete count of the population. For example, the census conducted by the government to collect information about the population of the country.

text: What is the main advantage of using a sample method?
options: It is time-consuming and expensive
It is less time-consuming and less expensive
It is more accurate and reliable
It is less accurate and reliable
correctAnswer: It is less time-consuming and less expensive
explanation: A sample method is a method of collecting data from a small part of the population. It is less time-consuming and less expensive compared to the census method. For example, a survey conducted by a researcher to collect information about the consumer behaviour.

text: What is the purpose of classification of data?
options: To present the data in a simple and easy to understand format
To make the data more complex and difficult to understand
To identify the patterns and trends in the data
To make the data more accurate and reliable
correctAnswer: To identify the patterns and trends in the data
explanation: Classification of data is the process of grouping the data into different categories. It helps to identify the patterns and trends in the data. For example, classifying the data on the basis of age, sex, income, etc.

text: What is the purpose of frequency distribution?

To identify the patterns and trends in the data
To make the data more complex and difficult to understand
To make the data more accurate and reliable
correctAnswer: To identify the patterns and trends in the data
explanation: Frequency distribution is a table that shows the number of observations in each category. It helps to identify the patterns and trends in the data. For example, a frequency distribution table that shows the number of people in each age group.
